planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring once soil has warmed, into humus-rich woodland soil; allow a season to establish before expecting bloom.

directions: This low, stoloniferous Japanese woodland perennial forms a creeping mat of rounded, leathery leaves marbled in silvery-gray along the veins, resembling a tortoiseshell pattern. In autumn it sends up thin wiry stems topped with small tufted white flower heads that have a fuzzy, dandelion-like texture, held just above the foliage. It spreads gradually by surface runners to form a loose groundcover and is best used as a textural filler among ferns, Asarum, and other woodland companions rather than as a solo specimen. Give it consistently moist, well-drained, acidic humus and dappled to full shade, and avoid root disturbance once established.
sources: NARGS (North American Rock Garden Society) seed exchange records
